ITEM PARAGRAPHS
When
a
candle
burns
,
the
flame
heats
the
nearby
air
and
starts
to
rise
.
This
warm
air
moves
up
,
cooler
air
and
oxygen
rush
in
at
the
bottom
of
the
flame
to
replace
it
.
When
that
cooler
air
is
heated
,
it
too
rises
up
and
is
replaced
by
cooler
air
at
the
base
of
the
flame
.
This
creates
a
continual
cycle
of
upward-moving
air
around
the
flame
(
a
convection
current
)
,
which
gives
the
flame
its
elongated
or
teardrop
shape
.
